concerns.advisory: The exit-code contract for `update-compatibility check` changes incompatibly: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` moves from 4 to 3 while 4 is simultaneously reused for the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` meaning, so any existing script or automation that branches on exit code 4 will now silently interpret a "feature disabled" failure as "recreate upgrade required".

Because the exit-code values changed, an operator (or CI pipeline) built against the new constants can be paired with an older Keycloak server image that still returns 4 for "recreate", producing a wrong upgrade decision during version skew.
concerns.why: CompatibilityResult exit-code renumbering is a runtime-observable contract between the operator/scripts and the `kc.sh update-compatibility` binary, which are versioned independently.

concerns.advisory: Nothing in the diff teaches the operator to recognize the new `FEATURE_DISABLED` (4) exit code, so when a user sets `update.strategy` without enabling `rolling-updates` the failure surfaces as a generic operator error rather than an actionable message — the docs only mitigate this with a CAUTION admonition.
concerns.why: New `FEATURE_DISABLED` constant plus docs text "Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail." in docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc; no operator-side handling added.

concerns.advisory: The new tests assert only the stderr message for the feature-disabled path and never assert the exit codes, so the renumbered `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE=3` and the new `FEATURE_DISABLED=4` are untested and could regress unnoticed.
concerns.why: UpdateCommandDistTest.testFeatureNotEnabled only calls `cliResult.assertError(...)`; testWrongVersions asserts messages but no exit code; only testCompatible asserts `assertEquals(0, result.exitCode())`.

concerns.advisory: The feature guard is duplicated at the top of each concrete command's `run()` instead of living in the shared `AbstractUpdatesCommand`, so any future `update-compatibility` subcommand will silently ship ungated unless the author remembers to copy the check.
concerns.why: Identical 5-line `if (!Profile.isFeatureEnabled(...)) { printFeatureDisabled(); picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED); return; }` block added to both UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() and UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run(), while `printFeatureDisabled()` was added to the shared base class.

concerns.advisory: The shared docs template now hardcodes `--features=rolling-updates` into every rendered `update-compatibility` example, which will have to be reverted across all generated docs when the feature graduates out of preview or becomes enabled by default.
concerns.why: docs/guides/templates/kc.adoc `updatecompatibility` macro appends `--features=rolling-updates` to the command line for all callers.

concerns.advisory: The sample custom-image Dockerfile now bakes the preview `rolling-updates` feature into the build layer unconditionally, so users who copy this reference image get a preview feature permanently enabled (and cannot turn it off without a rebuild), and it will override/conflict with any `--features` they add themselves.

The operator integration test now replaces the CR's entire enabled-features list rather than appending, so if the base test deployment or a future test needs another feature, this helper will silently drop it.

`ROLLING_UPDATES` is registered as `Type.PREVIEW`, which means it is also implicitly turned on by the blanket `--features=preview` switch even though all documentation instructs users to enable it by its specific name — worth confirming that is the intended activation surface for a feature that changes upgrade semantics.
concerns.why: common/.../Profile.java adds `ROLLING_UPDATES("Rolling Updates", Type.PREVIEW)`, while docs/tests exclusively use `--features=rolling-updates`.
